review.plain: An officer who wilfully and corruptly refuses or delays to execute process to apprehend or confine a person, so that the person escapes, faces a fine up to $500 or up to one year in prison.
acts: refuses to execute a lawful process directed to him and requiring him to apprehend or confine a person convicted of or charged with crime
omits or delays to execute such process

shared.who: An officer authorized to serve process

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to $500 or imprisonment for up to 1 year

crimes.act: Refuses to execute a lawful process directed to him and requiring him to apprehend or confine a person convicted of or charged with crime
conditions: The person escapes as a result

review.plain: Refusing or neglecting to help a sheriff, constable, police officer or watchman who requires it in a criminal case or to keep the peace is punishable by a fine up to $50 or up to one month in prison.
acts: neglects or refuses to assist him in the execution of his office in a criminal case, in the preservation of the peace or in the apprehension or securing of a person for a breach of the peace, or in a case of escape or rescue of persons arrested upon civil process

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to $50 or imprisonment for up to 1 month

crimes.act: Neglects or refuses to assist him in the execution of his office in a criminal case, in the preservation of the peace or in the apprehension or securing of a person for a breach of the peace, or in a case of escape or rescue of persons arrested upon civil process
conditions: The person is required in the name of the commonwealth by a sheriff, deputy sheriff, constable, police officer or watchman

review.plain: Refusing or neglecting to obey a justice of the peace who requires you to apprehend an offender is punished as set in the preceding section; ignorance of the justice's office is no excuse.
acts: refuses or neglects to obey such justice

crimes.act: Refuses or neglects to obey such justice
conditions: The person is required by a justice of the peace, upon view of a breach of the peace or of any other offence proper for his cognizance, to apprehend the offender
defenses: No person to whom such justice is known or declares himself to be a justice of the peace shall plead any excuse on pretence of ignorance of his office

penalties.penalty: Set in the preceding section

review.plain: Giving, selling or delivering alcoholic beverages to a prisoner, or possessing them at a prison to deliver to a prisoner, is punishable by a fine up to $50 or up to two months in prison.
acts: gives, sells or delivers alcoholic beverages, as defined in section one of chapter one hundred and thirty-eight, to a person confined in any correctional institution or other place of confinement, or to a person in the custody of a sheriff, constable, police officer, superintendent of a correctional institution, or other superintendent or keeper of a place of confinement
has in his possession, within the precincts of any prison or other place of confinement, any such beverages

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to $50 or imprisonment for up to 2 months

crimes.act: Gives, sells or delivers alcoholic beverages to a person confined in any correctional institution or other place of confinement, or to a person in the custody of a sheriff, constable, police officer, superintendent of a correctional institution, or other superintendent or keeper of a place of confinement
exceptions: Under the direction of the physician appointed to attend such prisoner

crimes.act: Has in his possession, within the precincts of any prison or other place of confinement, any such beverages
exceptions: Under the direction of the physician appointed to attend such prisoner
intent: With intent to convey or deliver them to any person confined therein

review.plain: Giving, selling or delivering alcoholic beverages to a patient or inmate of a public institution, or possessing them there to consume or pass on, is punishable by a fine up to $50 or up to two months in prison.
acts: gives, sells or delivers any alcoholic beverages, as defined in section one of chapter one hundred and thirty-eight, to any patient or inmate of any public institution, or to any patient or inmate under the control of any such institution
has in his possession within the precincts of any such institution any such beverages

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to $50 or imprisonment for up to 2 months

crimes.act: Gives, sells or delivers any alcoholic beverages to any patient or inmate of any public institution, or to any patient or inmate under the control of any such institution
exceptions: Under the direction of a physician authorized so to do

crimes.act: Has in his possession within the precincts of any such institution any such beverages
intent: With intent to consume the same or to convey, give, sell or deliver the same to any patient or inmate thereof

review.plain: Giving or delivering any drug or article to a prisoner, or possessing one at a prison to give to a prisoner, without permission is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison.
acts: gives or delivers to a prisoner in any correctional institution, or in any jail or house of correction, any drug or article whatever
has in his possession within the precincts of any prison herein named

penalties.penalty: Up to 5 years in state prison, up to 2 years in a jail or house of correction, or a fine of up to $1,000

crimes.act: Gives or delivers to a prisoner in any correctional institution, or in any jail or house of correction, any drug or article whatever
exceptions: With the permission of the superintendent or keeper

crimes.act: Has in his possession within the precincts of any prison herein named
exceptions: With the permission of the superintendent or keeper
intent: With intent to give or deliver to any prisoner any such drug or article

review.plain: A sheriff, jailer or correctional officer who gives or permits alcohol to a prisoner, or keeps prisoners of different sexes or classes together, forfeits $25 or $50 and is removed from office on a second conviction.
acts: gives, sells or delivers or knowingly permits to be given, sold or delivered to a prisoner in his custody any alcoholic beverages
willingly or negligently suffers such prisoner to have or drink any alcoholic beverages
places or keeps together prisoners in his custody of different sexes or classes

shared.who: A sheriff, jailer, superintendent of a house of correction or officer of a correctional institution

penalties.penalty: Forfeit $25

penalties.if: the offence is committed after a first conviction
penalties.penalty: Forfeit $50

consequences: Upon a second conviction, removal from office and ineligibility to hold the office of sheriff, deputy sheriff, jailer, superintendent or keeper of any correctional institution for five years thereafter

crimes.act: Gives, sells or delivers or knowingly permits to be given, sold or delivered to a prisoner in his custody any alcoholic beverages or cider
ways: knowingly permits to be given, sold or delivered
exceptions: The physician of the penal institution certifies in writing that the health of the prisoner requires the same

crimes.act: Willingly or negligently suffers such prisoner to have or drink any alcoholic beverages
exceptions: The physician certifies that the health of the prisoner requires such liquor, in which case the prisoner is allowed the quantity prescribed and no more

crimes.act: Places or keeps together prisoners in his custody of different sexes or classes
conditions: Contrary to the section of chapter one hundred and twenty-seven named in this section

review.plain: Wilfully disturbing a correctional institution or jail, or trying to attract the attention of or communicating with an inmate without permission, is punishable by a fine up to $50 or up to three months in prison.
acts: wilfully disturbs any correctional institution of the commonwealth
seeks to attract the attention of, or without the permission of the officer in charge has communication with, an inmate thereof

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to $50 or imprisonment for up to 3 months

crimes.act: Disturbs any correctional institution of the commonwealth, the Lyman school, industrial school for boys, industrial school for girls, or a jail or house of correction
Seeks to attract the attention of, or without the permission of the officer in charge has communication with, an inmate thereof
ways: seeks to attract the attention of an inmate
has communication with an inmate without the permission of the officer in charge

review.plain: Delivering or hiding articles for inmates, or taking articles from inmates, against institution rules is punishable by up to 3 years in state prison; an inmate bringing in drugs or weapons from furlough gets an added 7 to 10 years.
acts: delivers or procures to be delivered, or has in his possession with intent to deliver, to an inmate confined in any penal institution

deposits or conceals in or about the institution, or the dependencies thereof, or upon any land appurtenant thereto, or in any boat or vehicle going into the premises belonging to the institution, any article
receives from an inmate any article
brings or attempts to bring into said institution an illegal drug, gun, knife or other similar weapon

crimes.act: Delivers or procures to be delivered, or has in his possession with intent to deliver, to an inmate confined in any penal institution
ways: has in his possession with intent to deliver
conditions: Contrary to the rules and regulations of the institution
exceptions: With the knowledge and permission of the commissioner of correction or of the superintendent, keeper, sheriff or other officer in charge

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to $500, imprisonment in the state prison for up to 3 years, or in jail for up to 2½ years

crimes.act: Deposits or conceals in or about the institution, or the dependencies thereof, or upon any land appurtenant thereto, or in any boat or vehicle going into the premises belonging to the institution, any article
conditions: Contrary to the rules and regulations of the institution
exceptions: With the knowledge and permission of the commissioner of correction or of the superintendent, keeper, sheriff or other officer in charge
intent: With intent that an inmate shall obtain or receive it

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to $500, imprisonment in the state prison for up to 3 years, or in jail for up to 2½ years

crimes.act: Receives from an inmate any article
conditions: Contrary to the rules and regulations of the institution
exceptions: With the knowledge and permission of the commissioner of correction or of the superintendent, keeper, sheriff or other officer in charge
intent: With intent to convey it out of the institution

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to $500, imprisonment in the state prison for up to 3 years, or in jail for up to 2½ years

crimes.act: Brings or attempts to bring into said institution an illegal drug, gun, knife or other similar weapon
conditions: The inmate is returning from a furlough or a work program
crimes.who: An inmate of a correctional institution

penalties.penalty: An additional sentence of not less than 7 nor more than 10 years in state prison

review.plain: Opening, tampering with or damaging a police or fire signal box, or a highway emergency call box, is punishable by up to 2 years in prison for police and fire boxes, or a fine for call boxes.
acts: opens a signal box connected with a police signal system
interferes in any way with such box by breaking, cutting, injuring or defacing the same
opens, tampers or meddles with such box, or with any part or parts thereof, or with the police signal wires, or with anything connected therewith
tampers or meddles with a signal box connected with a fire signal system or with any part or thing connected therewith
opens a motorist highway emergency aid call box on any state highway connected with a highway emergency signal system
opens, tampers or meddles with such box, or with any part or parts thereof, or with anything connected therewith
tampers or meddles with a motorist highway emergency aid call box or with any part or thing connected therewith

crimes.act: Opens a signal box connected with a police signal system
intent: For the purpose of giving, or causing to be given, a false alarm

penalties.penalty: A fine of not less than $500 nor more than $1,000, imprisonment for up to 2 years, or both

crimes.act: Interferes in any way with such box by breaking, cutting, injuring or defacing the same
conditions: The box is connected with a police signal system

penalties.penalty: A fine of not less than $500 nor more than $1,000, imprisonment for up to 2 years, or both

crimes.act: Opens, tampers or meddles with such box, or with any part or parts thereof, or with the police signal wires, or with anything connected therewith
conditions: Without authority
The box is connected with a police signal system

penalties.penalty: A fine of not less than $500 nor more than $1,000, imprisonment for up to 2 years, or both

crimes.act: Tampers or meddles with a signal box connected with a fire signal system or with any part or thing connected therewith

penalties.penalty: A fine of not less than $500 nor more than $1,000, imprisonment for up to 2 years, or both

crimes.act: Opens a motorist highway emergency aid call box on any state highway connected with a highway emergency signal system
intent: For the purpose of giving or causing to be given a false call for aid

penalties.penalty: A fine of not less than $100 nor more than $500

crimes.act: Interferes in any way with such box by breaking, cutting, injuring or defacing the same
conditions: The box is a motorist highway emergency aid call box

penalties.penalty: A fine of not less than $100 nor more than $500

crimes.act: Opens, tampers or meddles with such box, or with any part or parts thereof, or with anything connected therewith
conditions: Without authority
The box is a motorist highway emergency aid call box

penalties.penalty: A fine of not less than $100 nor more than $500

crimes.act: Tampers or meddles with a motorist highway emergency aid call box or with any part or thing connected therewith

penalties.penalty: A fine of not less than $100 nor more than $500

review.plain: Willfully obstructing, interfering with or hindering a fire fighter or fire fighting force in the lawful performance of duty is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison.
acts: obstructs, interferes with or hinders a fire fighter in the lawful performance of his duty
obstructs, interferes with or hinders a fire fighting force in the lawful performance of its duty

penalties.penalty: A fine of not less than $100 nor more than $1,000, or imprisonment in a jail or house of correction for not less than 30 days nor more than 2½ years, or imprisonment in the state prison for up to 5 years, or both such fine and imprisonment in a jail or house of correction

crimes.act: Obstructs, interferes with or hinders a fire fighter or a fire fighting force in the lawful performance of his or its duty
conditions: The fire fighter or fire fighting force is in the lawful performance of duty

review.plain: Knowingly preventing or trying to prevent a police officer from making an arrest by force, threats, or other means creating a substantial risk of bodily injury is punishable by up to 2½ years in a house of correction.
acts: prevents or attempts to prevent a police officer, acting under color of his official authority, from effecting an arrest of the actor or another
using or threatening to use physical force or violence against the police officer or another
using any other means which creates a substantial risk of causing bodily injury to such police officer or another

terms: "Police officer": a police officer in uniform or, if out of uniform, one who has identified himself by exhibiting his credentials as such police officer while attempting such arrest

"Under color of official authority": when, in the regular course of assigned duties, he is called upon to make, and does make, a judgment in good faith based upon surrounding facts and circumstances that an arrest should be made by him

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in a jail or house of correction for up to 2½ years, a fine of up to $500, or both

crimes.act: Prevents or attempts to prevent a police officer, acting under color of his official authority, from effecting an arrest of the actor or another, by using or threatening to use physical force or violence against the police officer or another
defenses: Not a defense that the police officer was attempting to make an unlawful arrest, if he was acting under color of his official authority and was not resorting to unreasonable or excessive force giving rise to the right of self-defense

crimes.act: Prevents or attempts to prevent a police officer, acting under color of his official authority, from effecting an arrest of the actor or another, by using any other means which creates a substantial risk of causing bodily injury to such police officer or another
defenses: Not a defense that the police officer was attempting to make an unlawful arrest, if he was acting under color of his official authority and was not resorting to unreasonable or excessive force giving rise to the right of self-defense

review.plain: Falsely pretending to be a justice of the peace, notary, sheriff, police officer or other listed official or federal officer, and acting as one or demanding aid, is punishable by a fine up to $1,000 or up to 2½ years in prison.
acts: falsely assumes or pretends to be a justice of the peace, notary public, sheriff, deputy sheriff, medical examiner, associate medical examiner, constable, police officer, probation officer, or examiner, investigator or other officer appointed by the registrar of motor vehicles, or inspector, investigator or examiner of the department of public utilities or the department of telecommunications and cable, or investigator or other officer of the alcoholic beverages control commission, or investigator or other official of the bureau of special investigations, or examiner, investigator or other officer of the department of revenue or an officer or employee acting under the authority of the United States or any department, agency or officer thereof

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to $1,000 or imprisonment for up to 2½ years

crimes.act: Falsely assumes or pretends to be a justice of the peace, notary public, sheriff, deputy sheriff, medical examiner, associate medical examiner, constable, police officer, probation officer, or examiner, investigator or other officer appointed by the registrar of motor vehicles, or inspector, investigator or examiner of the department of public utilities or the department of telecommunications and cable, or investigator or other officer of the alcoholic beverages control commission, or investigator or other official of the bureau of special investigations, or examiner, investigator or other officer of the department of revenue or an officer or employee acting under the authority of the United States or any department, agency or officer thereof
conditions: The person acts as such or requires a person to aid or assist him in a matter pertaining to the duty of such officer

review.plain: Conducting a lead paint inspection without a license, or falsely holding yourself out as a licensed inspector, is punishable by a fine up to $5,000, up to one year in jail, or both.
acts: engages in or conducts a lead paint inspection without being licensed to do so
holds himself out to the public as a licensed lead paint inspector and is not so licensed

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to $5,000, imprisonment in jail for up to 1 year, or both

crimes.act: Engages in or conducts a lead paint inspection without being licensed to do so
Holds himself out to the public as a licensed lead paint inspector and is not so licensed

review.plain: Wearing a disguise with intent to obstruct the law or to intimidate or hinder an officer or person in lawful duties or rights is punishable by a fine up to $500 or up to one year in prison.
acts: disguises himself

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to $500 or imprisonment for up to 1 year

crimes.act: Disguises himself
conditions: It does not matter whether such intent is effected or not
intent: With intent to obstruct the due execution of the law, or to intimidate, hinder or interrupt an officer or other person in the lawful performance of his duty, or in the exercise of his rights under the constitution or laws of the commonwealth
consequences: If imprisoned, may also be bound to good behavior for one year after the expiration of the imprisonment

review.plain: Knowingly and willfully giving a false name or other identifying information to a law enforcement officer after an arrest is punishable by a fine up to $1,000 or up to one year in a house of correction.
acts: furnishes a false name, Social Security number, date of birth, home address, mailing address or phone number, or other information as may be requested for the purposes of establishing the person's identity, to a law enforcement officer or law enforcement official following an arrest

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to $1,000, imprisonment in a house of correction for up to 1 year, or both

consequences: The sentence runs from and after any sentence imposed as a result of the underlying offense
The court may order that restitution be paid to persons whose identity has been assumed and who have suffered monetary losses as a result of a violation

crimes.act: Furnishes a false name, Social Security number, date of birth, home address, mailing address or phone number, or other information as may be requested for the purposes of establishing the person's identity, to a law enforcement officer or law enforcement official following an arrest

review.plain: Without authority, using a town seal to make something look official, or making or possessing a badge like a town officer's with intent to assume an official character, is punishable by a fine up to $50.
acts: prints, stamps, engraves or affixes, or causes to be printed, stamped, engraved or affixed to any paper or other article a representation of the seal of a town in the commonwealth

casts, stamps, engraves, makes or has in his possession a badge or thing in the likeness of an official badge of a police officer, member of a fire department, or other officer appointed by a town in the commonwealth, or by any department of such town

penalties.penalty: A fine of up to $50

crimes.act: Prints, stamps, engraves or affixes, or causes to be printed, stamped, engraved or affixed to any paper or other article a representation of the seal of a town in the commonwealth
ways: causes to be printed, stamped, engraved or affixed
conditions: Without being duly authorized thereto
intent: With intent to give to such paper or article an official character which it does not possess

crimes.act: Casts, stamps, engraves, makes or has in his possession a badge or thing in the likeness of an official badge of a police officer, member of a fire department, or other officer appointed by a town in the commonwealth, or by any department of such town
conditions: Without being duly authorized thereto
intent: With intent to assume an official character which he does not possess

review.plain: Taking money or a reward under an agreement to conceal a felony or not prosecute or give evidence is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison if the felony carries death or life, otherwise up to 2 years in jail.
acts: takes money, or a gratuity or reward, or an engagement therefor, upon an agreement or understanding, express or implied, to compound or conceal such felony, or not to prosecute therefor, or not to give evidence thereof

crimes.act: Takes money, or a gratuity or reward, or an engagement therefor, upon an agreement or understanding, express or implied, to compound or conceal such felony, or not to prosecute therefor, or not to give evidence thereof
knowledge: Having knowledge of the commission of a felony

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in the state prison for up to 5 years or in jail for up to 1 year

penalties.if: such crime is punishable in any other manner
penalties.penalty: A fine of up to $500 or imprisonment in jail for up to 2 years

review.plain: Knowingly making a false written statement under penalty of perjury to police or the registry alleging a motor vehicle theft is punishable by up to 2 years, or 1 to 5 years for a repeat offense.
acts: makes a false written statement on a form bearing notice that false statements made therein are punishable under the penalty of perjury, to a police officer, police department or the registry of motor vehicles alleging the theft or conversion of a motor vehicle

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment for not less than 5 months nor more than 2 years, a fine of not less than $250 and not more than $2,500, or both

penalties.if: the person is found guilty for a second or subsequent offense
penalties.penalty: Imprisonment for not less than 1 nor more than 5 years, a fine of not less than $500 and not more than $5,000, or both; the sentence shall not be reduced to less than one year

consequences: For a second or subsequent offense, not eligible for probation, parole, furlough or work release, except a temporary release granted by the commissioner of correction to attend the funeral of next of kin or spouse, visit a critically ill close relative or spouse, or obtain emergency medical services unavailable at the institutions
A prosecution under this section shall neither be continued without a finding nor placed on file

crimes.act: Makes a false written statement on a form bearing notice that false statements made therein are punishable under the penalty of perjury, to a police officer, police department or the registry of motor vehicles alleging the theft or conversion of a motor vehicle

review.plain: A person who knows another is a victim of rape, murder, manslaughter or armed robbery and is at the scene must report it to law enforcement when safe, or face a fine of $500 to $2,500.
acts: report said crime to an appropriate law enforcement official as soon as reasonably practicable

penalties.penalty: A fine of not less than $500 nor more than $2,500

crimes.act: Fails to report said crime to an appropriate law enforcement official as soon as reasonably practicable
conditions: The person is at the scene of said crime
exceptions: The person cannot report without danger or peril to himself or others
knowledge: Knowing that another person is a victim of aggravated rape, rape, murder, manslaughter or armed robbery
